label: The ablative absolute
notes: When the participle's noun plays NO part in the main clause, both go into the ablative and the phrase stands apart: Urbe captā, 'the city having been captured'. Translate loosely — 'when/since/after/although the city was captured' — and let the context choose. If the noun already has a job in the main clause, use an ordinary agreeing participle instead.

cells.tell: a noun and participle in the ablative, grammatically free of the sentence

examples.translation: The city having been captured, everyone departed.

fakes.teaches: Urbem is ACCUSATIVE — then the phrase would be the object of the main verb. The ablative is what cuts it loose from the sentence.
